summary: Lattice observation tower in Talladega National Forest, Hale County, Alabama; NHLR-registered January 2026; in great condition as of August 2025 per the register.

facts.status_note: The register says it was in great condition as of August 2025, but also that Forest Service volunteers at the recreation area did not know whether it was still standing

visit.trail_note: Off an unmarked Forest Service road; the register describes a three-quarter-mile hike

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Alabama Mound Trail page calls the Payne Lake area a microcosm of the Oakmulgee National Forest and also places it in the Talladega National Forest. The Register and the 1980 map place the tower in the Talladega National Forest, and the story follows them.

notes_for_editor: Build date, builder and staffing are unknown; no source gives them. Beyond the 2026 register entry, the history is one 1980 map listing and OpenStreetMap tags. The register's great-condition report is dated August 2025, and the same entry says volunteers did not know whether it still stands, so status is the main uncertainty. Access and drive-up facts come from the register only; check before any visit. Do not confuse this with the Payne Lake Dam control tower in Forest Service project 60498 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/alabama/projects/60498), which is a different structure. Elevation differs: NHLR 477 ft (145 m) vs OpenStreetMap ele 153 m; the brief's 145.4 m matches NHLR. The register credits a photo to Brendon Minchew, but its image URL was not captured, so no photos were added.
